about: Question 10 (A), decided by the owner on 2026-09-16. Control test 4.7 holds today's engine to this written prediction of how its capture of the control corpus differs from the stored control capture (tools/control-corpus.json, controlCapture): every difference with its kind, scenario, path, and reference and candidate values, exactly as tools/differential-harness.js reports them. A difference found and not declared, or declared and not found, fails 4.7; a category or a pattern approves nothing. An output-moving commit declares its differences here, with its reason under changes, before it lands. Historical integrity, whether the stored capture is what its own engine computed, is a separate check (tools/historical-replay.js).

changes.change: S5 audit round R5, S5R-04 (Q85): a recurring income stops at its owner's end age, prorated within the row (the owner's answer 3 (A) of 2026-09-16)
changes.why: Before it, an income paid in full in the row that starts at its end age. Every control difference follows from that row: in each of the 13 scenarios below, one or two incomes with a whole-number end age paid one more year; their row income falls by that year's payment, and totals, taxes, withdrawals, spending, shortfalls and failure ages follow.
changes.verified: Before the commit, from the parent's plans and captures: the scenarios that move and the first row each moves at are exactly those an income end age cuts, and in the 11 simple- and historical-mode scenarios each cut row's income change equals the parent's own stream amount times the fraction the end age removes (14 rows). The two Monte Carlo scenarios (seed:9, seed:17) are checked by scenario and first row only.

changes.change: S5 audit round R6, S5 task 8 on the owner's question 5, answer (C), landed after question 10 (A): Arizona's age-65 exemption, basic standard deduction record and Social Security subtraction
changes.why: Arizona taxable income is now reduced by $2,100 for each person 65 or older, never below zero, which lowers the Arizona tax by up to $52.50 a person a year; balances, withdrawals, taxes, MAGI, required distributions and shortfalls follow. The deduction record and the Social Security subtraction reproduce the prior Arizona base exactly.
changes.verified: Before the commit: with the exemption set to $0 the candidate reproduces its parent exactly on both compositions (so the exemption is the only output-moving part), the original figures of every re-derived test pass at $0, the golden fixture regenerated at $0 is byte-identical to the parent's, every scenario R6 moves first moves at or after a row where someone is 65 or older, and this cumulative list is exactly R5's declaration composed with R6's own movement.

changes.why: Every row of every scenario gains federalAgi, ssProvisionalIncome, seniorDeductionMagi, niitMagi and irmaaMagi, each an EXTRA_FIELD against the control, which predates contract version 3. No existing field changes.

changes.change: S5AA task 2.1 (Q108): the carried spending base is the UNADJUSTED amount, so a stage adjusts the year it applies to instead of becoming the next year's starting point.
changes.why: applyStage() was inside both branches of the carried base, and fixedReal computes each year as priorSpend*inflationStep, so the adjustment re-applied to its own output every year. A 50% stage halved every year and never recovered after its window; an amount stage became the permanent level. Only fixedReal carries a base forward, so only fixedReal scenarios move. In the control corpus exactly one generated scenario has stages under fixedReal (seed:6, an amount stage over ages 49-61 and an 83.67% stage over 62-69); its differences move accordingly, and the differences the old behaviour produced at later rows no longer occur.

changes.change: S5AA task 2.2 (Q109): the down-year flexibility cut is a level, not a ratchet -- it no longer writes into the carried spending base.
changes.why: base*=1-flexibility/100 wrote the cut into what the next year starts from, so each cut was taken from the previous year's already-cut figure (80,000 -> 72,000 -> 64,800 -> 58,320 -> 52,488, never recovering). The policy itself is unchanged and is written out in Handover temp/S5AA_FLEXIBILITY_POLICY_20260920.md: same signal, same one-period lookback, same strictly-negative trigger, same stage and inflation interaction. Only fixedReal carries a base forward, and the cut only fires on a negative prior return, so the scenarios that move are exactly the fixedReal members whose method can produce one AND whose flexibility is above zero: seed:8, seed:11, seed:18 and the three targeted historical starts (1929, 1966, 2000). fixedReal members on the simple method (seed:6, seed:13, seed:19) hold a constant positive return and correctly do not move.

changes.change: S5AA task 3.1 (Q88, F2 with G16): the age-65 additional standard deduction under IRC 63(f) is applied, per qualifying person by their own age, beside the enhanced senior deduction.
changes.why: The IRC 63(f) additional standard deduction for the aged was missing from the engine entirely: estimateTaxes() charged the basic standard deduction plus the temporary OBBBA enhanced senior deduction and nothing else, so a single 67-year-old was given $22,100 where Rev. Proc. 2025-32 section 4.14(3) gives $24,150. The citation was checked against the IRS PDF itself BEFORE the rule was coded, as task 8.6 requires; the check is recorded in Handover temp/S5AA_CITATION_CHECKS_20260920.md (C-01). taxSegmentLocal(), the funding solver's mirror, moved in the SAME COMMIT (ground rule 4, G16); because the 63(f) amount carries no phaseout it enters the mirror as a constant with zero slope. SCOPE, MEASURED EXHAUSTIVELY ACROSS ALL 36 MEMBERS RATHER THAN SAMPLED: a member moves if and only if some year at age 65 or over has federal AGI above the deduction that year ALREADY had. That is 24 members, with zero disagreements in either direction. The six that never reach 65 are unchanged to the cent, and six more reach 65 but have no federal taxable income for the new amount to reduce. seed:13 is the sharpest of those: it owes $78 in a senior year and still does not move, because every cent of that $78 is ARIZONA, whose base keeps its own $2,100 age-65 exemption and its own standard deduction record and never reads the federal figure -- and because its federal AGI of $19,213 sat below even the old $22,100 deduction.

changes.change: S5AA task 3.2 (Q89, F3 with G17): the net investment income tax base includes ordinary dividends and the rental and investment income streams Form 8960 Part I counts.
changes.why: Form 8960 Part I counts ordinary dividends (line 2), rental real estate (4a) and interest and gains (1, 5); the engine's NIIT base was capitalGains + qualifiedDividends only. The citation was checked against the IRS PDF itself BEFORE the rule was coded, as task 8.6 requires; the check and the full income mapping are in Handover temp/S5AA_CITATION_CHECKS_20260920.md (C-02). THE NAME IS A TRAP: Form 8960 line 2 means the TOTAL of all dividends, of which qualified are a subset, while the engine's ordinaryDividends is the NON-QUALIFIED REMAINDER. So the two ADD without double counting and their sum is exactly line 2. The surtax was given its OWN quantity rather than being added to investmentIncome, because the caller already folds ordinary dividends into ordinaryIncome: adding them to investmentIncome would have double counted them in federal AGI, the Social Security provisional base and the Arizona base, AND would have handed them the preferential capital-gains rate. Only the cap moved. SCOPE MEASURED BY DIFFERENTIAL COMPARISON, not against the stored reference, because matchPrediction keys a difference on (scenario, kind, path) and not on its value and is therefore blind to a task moving a path that an earlier task already moved. Against the same engine with the repair neutralised, exactly ONE member moves: seed:7, by +$463.82 across two years, every delta positive, with no row-count or error change anywhere. The others are explained rather than assumed: the surtax is 3.8% of the LESSER of net investment income and the MAGI excess, and in every above-threshold year of seed:3, seed:6 and seed:18 the existing base had ALREADY filled that cap -- seed:3 at age 68 carries $182,865 of base against a $15,558 excess -- so the added income is inert. seed:7 is the only member whose base sat BELOW its excess ($0 against $4,092).

changes.change: S5AA task 3.4 (Q98, G4): an employment-type income stream is routed into the wage payroll-tax base, keeping its owner, because the OASDI wage base is a per-person cap.
changes.why: An `employment`-type entry in retirement.otherIncomes is wages, and wages bear Social Security and Medicare payroll tax. The engine folded it into other.ordinary, so it already bore INCOME tax correctly, but it never reached the wage base and so bore no FICA at all: the same $60,000 cost $8,312.50 as employment.salary and $3,722.50 as a stream, a gap of exactly $4,590.00, which is 7.65% of it. estimateTaxes() takes ordinaryIncome and wages as SEPARATE parameters and uses wages only for payroll, so adding the stream to the wage channel does not double count it for income tax. THE OWNER IS KEPT, and that is the load-bearing part: the self's wages are derived as (wages - spouseWages) and each person's OASDI is capped separately, so crediting a spouse's job to the self would push both onto one cap and UNDERCHARGE a two-earner household -- the failure a household-total repair makes while every single-earner test still passes. SCOPE, measured differentially against the same engine with the repair neutralised: exactly the three members carrying an employment stream move -- seed:10 (self), seed:12 (spouse), seed:15 (household) -- every delta positive, none without such a stream, and none with one left unmoved. Row counts and calculation errors are unchanged everywhere. DISCLOSED: an owner of "household" is attributed to SELF and so takes one person's OASDI cap. That is not a choice made here -- seSelf/seSpouse already resolve it the same way, because only "spouse" is tested -- and splitting it would be new modelling.

changes.change: S5AA task 3.5 (Q104, G11): a cafeteria-plan HSA salary reduction leaves the FICA wage base, per owner and capped at that owner's wages; 401(k) deferrals and direct contributions do not.
changes.why: Publication 969: a contribution an employer makes using an employee's salary reduction THROUGH A CAFETERIA PLAN is treated as an employer contribution, and employer HSA contributions are not subject to social security or Medicare tax. The engine gave an HSA and a 401(k) deferral IDENTICAL answers -- $8,004.50 on $50,000 of wages either way -- when they should differ by FICA on the contribution. PRE-TAX IS NOT ONE CATEGORY, which is the whole finding. Three routes give three answers: an HSA cafeteria-plan salary reduction is out of income tax AND out of FICA; a DIRECT personal HSA contribution is an above-the-line deduction that cannot touch a wage-level tax; an ordinary 401(k) elective deferral is out of income tax but REMAINS WAGES. preTaxDeferrals deliberately mixes all three and feeds only the income tax base, so the HSA share is tracked separately and per owner. Per owner because OASDI is capped per person, and CAPPED AT THAT OWNER'S OWN WAGES because a salary reduction cannot exceed the salary. DISCLOSED: the engine has no cafeteria-plan flag, so it cannot express a DIRECT personal contribution; the exclusion is applied to the route it does model, and adding an input would be feature wiring. SCOPE, measured differentially: six members move -- seed:4, seed:5, seed:8, seed:9, seed:15, seed:19 -- and NOTHING without a contributing HSA moves. The six that have one and do not move are explained: four have no wages at all, and seed:7 and seed:13 have contributionStop equal to their starting age, so no contributing year exists. ON THE SIGN: the DIRECT effect is a reduction in every mover's first moved year (-682.81, -118.42, -340.38, -336.60, -403.59, -103.40, and seed:9's is exactly FICA on $4,400). seed:8's TOTAL is nonetheless +71.95, because less tax early leaves more invested and the larger portfolio pays more tax later: 4 years down and 22 up. The first-order sign is the claim, not the sum.

changes.change: S5AA task 4.4 (Q99, G5): the qualified-medical share of an HSA distribution
changes.why: NO NUMERIC OUTPUT MOVES. The share defaults to 100% -- every HSA draw assumed qualified, which is exactly what the engine did before -- so no corpus member, none of which carries the new field, changes a single balance, tax or total. Verified separately against HEAD's engine across all 36 members at 1e-9: zero field differences. What DOES appear is the disclosure the task requires: HSA_QUALIFIED_SHARE_ASSUMED, a WARNING recorded once by every plan that holds a health savings account, saying what is being assumed about its withdrawals and naming the statutory disability and death exceptions the engine does not model. Twelve of the 36 control members hold an HSA, so twelve gain one issue each. The default is what makes this a disclosure rather than a silent re-pricing of plans saved before the field existed.

changes.change: S5AA task 4.6 (Q91, F5 and N3): the Social Security retirement earnings test, and the adjustment of the reduction factor at full retirement age
changes.why: All four figures had been in the rules package since it was written and NOTHING READ THEM, so a household claiming before full retirement age while still working was paid in full. TWO control members move and the other thirty-four are explained. Of the five that claim before full retirement age with a retirement age past their claim, seed:2 and seed:10 have NO EARNINGS at all, and seed:4 starts the plan at 67 -- already full retirement age -- where earnings are not tested. seed:5 (claims at 64, works to 76, $247,369 of salary) and seed:20 (both spouses claim at 62 and work to 69, $148,808 between them) are the two the test can reach, and both are poorer for it. Benefits are withheld below full retirement age; the withheld MONTHS are then credited back against the reduction factor from full retirement age onward, which raises the benefit permanently. The differences run to the end of each horizon because that adjustment is permanent and every later balance compounds from it. Declarations for paths these two members had already moved under an earlier change are REPLACED, not duplicated.

changes.change: S5AA task 4.7 (Q92, F6 with G19): a survivor benefit from 60, reduced for age
changes.why: NO NUMERIC OUTPUT MOVES, and the reason is a gap in the corpus rather than an inert repair. Only TWO of the 36 members have survivor benefits on at all. seed:4 has its first death at self-age 85, which is its horizon end, so nobody is ever widowed inside it. targeted:survivor-stateful widows its survivor at 68 -- PAST survivor full retirement age, where the reduction factor is exactly 1. So neither the new age-60 floor nor the reduction can differ for any member, and the rule is pinned by its own tests alone. Logged as F-09. What DOES appear is the disclosure task 4.7 requires: SURVIVOR_BENEFIT_APPROXIMATED, a WARNING carrying a machine-readable approximation flag, recorded by each of the two members that model a survivor benefit, naming remarriage, disability, children and the deceased early-claim cap of POMS RS 00615.320 as not modelled.

changes.change: S5AA task 5.1 (Q94, F8): an adjustable-rate loan always re-amortises at its reset; the switch is retired
changes.why: NO NUMERIC OUTPUT MOVES, and the reason is a defect in the CORPUS rather than an inert repair. Five members carry a debt typed rateType "adjustable". FOUR of them -- seed:3, seed:7, seed:14, seed:17 -- have nextRateResetAge and resetRate UNDEFINED, so they are adjustable in name only and never reach a reset at all: the month test compares against undefined and is false forever. The fifth, targeted:arm-flag-on, is the one scenario built to set the old flag AND carry a resetting debt, so it already re-amortised and is unchanged. Logged as F-10, with the generator defect named separately. The single difference is the disclosure: ARM_RECAST_ALWAYS_APPLIED, recorded by a plan holding an adjustable debt that actually has a reset age, telling it the payment now rises at the reset where before it did not.

changes.change: S5AA task 5.5: the reference supported domain, made DETECTABLE at the engine boundary
changes.why: NO NUMERIC OUTPUT MOVES ANYWHERE. Three exclusions that were reachable from ordinary inputs and SILENT now record an issue carrying outsideSupportedDomain:true, the exclusion name, and the new-engine task that owns it -- a machine-readable fact a runner can filter on, which is what makes enforcement at a boundary possible at all. FOURTEEN of the 36 control members are outside the domain in at least one respect, and nothing said so before. Most are the Roth restriction: the engine models a Roth draw as free at every age, with no ordering stack, no basis and no five-year clock, so a plan that retires before 59 1/2 holding a Roth account is a reference only for QUALIFIED withdrawals -- and that includes golden:baseline itself, which retires at 55. Two members also carry the historical replay exclusion. The enforcement half is NOT done here and is owed to task 6.2: excluding affected members changes what the corpus covers and therefore its capture.

changes.change: S5AA task 3.6 STEP 2 (Q87, F1): Form 8606 per-owner IRA basis, and the pro-rata rule
changes.why: TWO members move, seed:4 and seed:9, and NEITHER holds a traditional IRA account -- so no basis is involved in either. The movement is entirely the funding solver preTax class becoming split PER ACCOUNT unconditionally, which reassociates the floating-point arithmetic of the tax-funding walk. Task 4.1 built that split CONDITIONALLY and named these exact two members as the ones it moved, and said in the engine comment that step 2 would have to make it unconditional because rIncome is where IRA basis enters and it varies per account. This is that, and it is a predicted movement rather than a surprise. The basis rule itself moves NOTHING here: no control member makes a nondeductible traditional IRA contribution, so the pro-rata fraction is zero for every one of them -- the same instrument gap as F-05.

changes.change: S5AA F-02 (Q88): the tax layer asks who is alive -- RECORDED RETROACTIVELY by the second S5AA audit
changes.why: This record was MISSING. F-02 (e63d606) replaced one declaration -- targeted:survivor-stateful, issues LENGTH, candidate 1 -> 2 -- and wrote no reason here, although this file's own rule is that an output-moving commit declares its reason under changes before it lands. The reason, reconstructed from that commit: the member widows at self-age 68 inside a horizon ending at 72, so it gains SURVIVOR_FILING_STATUS_MODELLED, the approximation F-02 raises wherever a filing transition happens inside the horizon. NO NUMERIC OUTPUT MOVES for it: both salaries are zero and its one account is a Roth, so the single brackets it reaches from 70 are applied to no taxable income.

changes.change: S5AA self-audit (33dc5bf): a household after a death is outside the supported domain -- RECORDED RETROACTIVELY by the second S5AA audit
changes.why: This record was MISSING for the same reason as the F-02 record above: 33dc5bf replaced one declaration -- targeted:survivor-stateful, issues LENGTH, candidate 2 -> 3 -- and gave its reason only in a commit message. The member gained UNSUPPORTED_POST_DEATH_HOUSEHOLD. THE SECOND AUDIT FOUND THAT ENTRY FALSE FOR THIS MEMBER: it told a household with two zero salaries and one Roth that "their employment income continues". See the next record.

changes.change: S5AA second audit: the post-death exclusion names only what is actually carried past a death
changes.why: targeted:survivor-stateful, issues LENGTH, candidate 3 -> 2: the member LOSES UNSUPPORTED_POST_DEATH_HOUSEHOLD, correctly. The entry was written to be raised where the deceased "holds an account or earns a wage", and tested the ENTERED salary and ANY balance. A salary ends at the retirement age on its earner's own clock whether or not anyone dies, and an account is mis-billed only where required distributions are on and the dead owner's own clock reaches the start age inside the horizon. This member's self dies at 68 with no salary and holds only a Roth, which has no required distribution -- nothing is carried past the death, and the old entry's prose was false for it. NO NUMERIC OUTPUT MOVES: the change is to an issue list, and the engine's arithmetic is untouched.

changes.change: S5AA follow-up, Q3 (4e97830): a deceased person's wages and contributions end at the death
changes.why: NO CONTROL MEMBER MOVES, and this record says so because a silent absence is how two records went missing before. The work duration now ends at the earner's death as it ends at retirement. No control member dies while still earning -- targeted:survivor-stateful has two zero salaries -- so nothing in the control can see it; the repair is pinned by tests/audit-s5aa-wages-end-at-death.test.js alone, and the gap is named in the close record.

changes.change: S5AA follow-up, Q4: a deceased spouse's accounts pass to the survivor from the year after the death
changes.why: targeted:survivor-stateful, issues LENGTH 2 -> 3, the declaration REPLACED: the member gains SPOUSAL_ROLLOVER_ASSUMED, the approximation raised wherever a spouse dies and the other survives to take the accounts (Treas. Reg. 1.408-8(c), IRC 402(c)(9)). NO NUMERIC OUTPUT MOVES: the self dies at 68 owning only a Roth, which has no required distribution, so passing it to the spouse changes who owns it and nothing that is computed from it. No control member holds a pre-tax account in the name of someone who dies -- the numeric half of Q4 is pinned by tests/audit-s5aa-spousal-rollover.test.js alone.

changes.change: S5AA third audit: Q3 completed -- one definition of each person's work duration; employment and self-employment streams end at their owner's death
changes.why: NO CONTROL MEMBER MOVES, and the expanded capture r4 is IDENTICAL (corpus hash 083a948a...). Two halves of Q3 that 4e97830 missed: ownerContributionEligibility() kept its own copy of the work rule and still counted a dead spouse eligible, so the dead spouse took part of the HSA family limit ahead of the survivor (MEASURED: $3,750 of a $5,000 request inside an $8,750 limit); and an employment or self-employment income stream kept paying after its owner's death. No control member has an HSA or an earned income stream with a death while working, so neither is visible here; both are pinned by tests/audit-s5aa-wages-end-at-death.test.js.

changes.change: S5AA R6 external audit: EA-01 -- a row in which nobody the plan models is alive is outside the supported domain, whatever is billed; EA-02 -- Medicare costs count the living only
changes.why: FIVE DIFFERENCES, ALL AN ISSUE COUNT, NO FIGURE MOVES. Every golden scenario is the default plan -- a household of one with a lifespan of 95 against a horizon of 100 -- so each now carries UNSUPPORTED_POST_DEATH_HOUSEHOLD for the rows opening at 96 to 99, which projected spending, withdrawals, tax and returns for nobody and said nothing (baseline, monte-carlo-fixed-seed, reserve-and-bond-tent and guardrails-withdrawal-strategy go from 1 issue to 2; rmd-and-roth-conversion from 0 to 1, and there the entry also names required distributions billed on the dead owner's age, which were silent). EA-02 moves no control member: none has health costs on with a couple and a death. Pinned by tests/audit-s5aa-r6-no-survivor.test.js and tests/audit-s5aa-r6-health-population.test.js.

changes.change: S5AA R7 re-audit: R7-01, R7-02, R7-03 and the fourth internal audit (A4-1, A4-4, A4-6) -- the death disclosures come from executed state
changes.why: NO CONTROL DIFFERENCE MOVES: every change is to an issue's order or content, and 4.7 compares the issue count. A CORRECTION TO THE EA-01 RECORD ABOVE: it said golden:rmd-and-roth-conversion's exclusion 'also names required distributions billed on the dead owner's age, which were silent'. That was false. The entry predicted billing from the configured accounts; MEASURED at 0088831, that scenario's pre-tax money is exhausted by 93 and nothing is billed after the death at 95. The entry now names only what was billed (A4-6), and for that scenario names nothing. The expanded capture moved in issues only: order, the F-02 wording (R7-01), the executed succession record (R7-02) -- no financial figure.

changes.change: S5AA R9 round: the owner's decision Q4, the dividends-on half (known item 5.2) -- with the dividend feature on, the entered yield is taxed in every year, not only once the cash is paid out
changes.why: SIX CONTROL MEMBERS MOVE, EACH WITH THE DIVIDEND FEATURE ON AND TAXABLE MONEY BEFORE THE PAYOUT STARTS: seed:2, seed:5, seed:13, seed:16, seed:18, seed:19. Before this, only the paid-out cash was taxed, so these households paid no dividend tax at all in their working years (seed:2's row 1 MAGI was 0 on $2.9M taxable); now the entered yield on the eligible taxable balance is taxed in those years at the entered qualified share, as a reinvested dividend is (IRC 61(a)(7)). Each member's lifetime taxes rise accordingly (seed:2 24,380 to 88,478; seed:18 1,316,361 to 1,682,813), and every downstream balance moves with the tax paid. After the payout starts nothing changes. Five declarations are dropped because seed:13's rows 14-15 now equal the control there. No golden scenario has the feature on, so no golden fixture moves. The dividends-OFF branch (the imputed 1.5%) is unchanged. Pinned by tests/audit-s5aa-r9-dividends-taxed-every-year.test.js.

changes.change: S5AA R9 round: the owner's decision 7 -- the survivor spending reduction reads householdSurvivorship(), so the row opening at a lifespan (the year of death) is spent for two
changes.why: ONE CONTROL MEMBER MOVES: targeted:survivor-stateful (self dies at 68, spouse alive, 25% survivor reduction). Its row opening at 68 was already reduced under strategySpending()'s own strict 'age < selfLife'; the engine's one definition, householdSurvivorship(), counts the self alive in that row -- the year of death, filed jointly and costed for two -- so it is now spent in full (rows[4].spending 50,937.98), and every later balance carries the one extra year of full spending. The reduction then applies from the row opening at 69, once, as before. No other member has the survivor adjustment on with a whole-year lifespan inside its horizon; no golden scenario has it on. Pinned by tests/audit-s5aa-r9-spending-survivor-boundary.test.js.

changes.change: S5AA R9 round: the owner's decision 8 -- the projection stops at the last death (PROJECTION_ENDS_AT_LAST_DEATH replaces the post-death exclusion)
changes.why: THE FIVE GOLDEN MEMBERS MOVE, AND NOTHING ELSE. Each is the default plan: a household of one with a lifespan of 95 against a horizon of 100. Its rows opening at 96 to 99 projected spending, withdrawals, tax and returns for nobody (EA-01 marked them outside the supported domain); they are no longer projected, so each capture ends at the row opening at 95, the year of the death (rows LENGTH 72 to 68; rmd-and-roth-conversion 33 to 29). Lifetime taxes fall by those four years (baseline 20,212,459 to 14,183,844). golden:monte-carlo-fixed-seed goes from failed=true / 99.8% to failed=false / 100%: its only failing paths ran out of money in the rows after the death, for a household that no longer existed; firstShortfallAge becomes null. The issue COUNT does not move: UNSUPPORTED_POST_DEATH_HOUSEHOLD is replaced one for one by PROJECTION_ENDS_AT_LAST_DEATH. 268 declarations on the rows that no longer exist are dropped. No seeded or targeted member reaches a last death inside its horizon. Pinned by tests/audit-s5aa-r9-stop-at-last-death.test.js; the golden fixtures are regenerated in the same commit.

changes.change: R10-01: the remaining-life strategies count the years the plan models
changes.why: External audit of 02b921a, finding R10-01: VPW and the RMD-style strategy divided by horizon - age + 1, one year more than the plan models. seed:17 is the control's only member using a remaining-life strategy (rmd, Monte Carlo, age 56 to 79): each year's draw rises by a factor of 24/23 at the opening, so the shortfall grows and the q90 band falls. The other members do not reach either strategy.

changes.change: R11-01: a drawn required distribution is held out of the row's return
changes.why: External re-audit of b053dc2, finding R11-01. Once a conversion or transfer draws on an obligation, its reserve is held out of the growth that runs before the distribution is paid, as though it were distributed before the conversion. golden:rmd-and-roth-conversion is the control's only member converting in RMD years (from 73, $20,000 a year): its reserve no longer earns the year's return, so pre-tax balances and later RMDs are lower, lifetime tax falls by $2,255 and totals by 0.6-0.7%; pass/fail and the success rate are unchanged. 209 declarations revised, 14 no longer differing from the reference, none added.

changes.change: S5AA R18 round, workstream B (R10-06): taxable basis in dollars, capital losses with a $3,000 offset and carry-forward, each account paying its own dividend
changes.why: A taxable account carried its basis as a percentage of its balance, so growth added basis and a later sale realised no gain; contributions and reinvested or imputed taxed dividends added none; a paid dividend took basis as if sold; losses could not exist; and the household dividend was taken from accounts in list order. Basis is now dollars (design reviewed by the external auditor; rulings B1 (c) and B2 adopted by the owner 2026-09-22). Measured headline movement per member is in the round's evidence (S5AA_R18_WORKSTREAM_B_HEADLINE_MOVEMENT.json): 36 of 61 expanded members change, every status stays ok, and pass/fail changes nowhere; seed:8, already at 0% success, fails one year earlier.

changes.change: S5AA R18 self-audit, finding SA18-01: the carryover a year uses is capped by taxable income
changes.why: The Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet (Schedule D instructions, lines 1-4; IRC 1212(b)(2)) counts a year's loss deduction as used only up to its taxable income before the loss. The engine treated the whole deduction as used, so a year under the standard deduction lost up to $3,000 of carryover; the kept carryover now offsets later gains, lowering later tax.

changes.change: S5AA R19, R18-01: a capital loss is deducted whatever the other income and lowers taxable Social Security
changes.why: ChatGPT's R18 external audit, R18-01 (P2): the deduction was capped at non-Social-Security ordinary income plus qualified dividends, so a loss with no other income never reached the Social Security Benefits Worksheet's line 3 (Form 1040 line 7a). Now min(3000, net loss) whatever the other income; qualified dividends stay preferential up to taxable income; NII includes the loss (Form 8960 line 5a); AGI may be negative, as Form 1040 line 11 may (the owner, 2026-09-23).

changes.change: S5AA R19, workstream A: the tax-liability ledger's row fields (result-contract version 5)
changes.why: Workstream A (R10-03/04/05; contract reviewed in ChatGPT's R18 audit; built on the owner's decision of 2026-09-23) adds taxSettled, taxTrueUpPaid and taxOutstanding to every deterministic row. No control member holds IRA basis or a post-70.5 QCD offset, so no value moves: taxSettled equals taxes and the true-up fields are 0 on every row (the contract's identity 4). The differences are the new fields only.

changes.change: S5AA R20, R18F-01: a glide path's return and risk come from one allocation
changes.why: ChatGPT's R18 full-model audit, R18-01 (P1; renumbered R18F-01), repaired on the owner's decision of 2026-09-23. accountVolatility() read the opening allocation while accountExpected() moved the stock weight along the glide, so a Monte Carlo draw paired the glided mean with the opening risk. Both now read accountGlideWeights(); an all-stock account glides into bonds (the owner). seed:9 is the one control member with a glide under Monte Carlo: its two large 401(k)s glide down to 31% stocks (volatility 15.6% and 11.2% at the start, 6.2% and 6.3% at retirement), its HSAs and Roth glide up. Success stays 100%; median lifetime tax 5,415,750.51 -> 5,586,268.95. No other member moves (seed:20 glides in simple mode, where only the expected return is read, and every account holds a non-stock sleeve).

changes.change: S5AA R23, R22-01: the Roth exclusion follows an actual draw by the owner's age
changes.why: UNSUPPORTED_ROTH_ORDERING was raised from inputs; it is now raised where a Roth dollar is drawn before its owner is 59 1/2. Six control scenarios never drew a Roth dollar early and lose the flag (one issue fewer each); no figure moves.

changes.change: S5AA R26: IRA contributions are capped at taxable compensation
changes.why: IRS Publication 590-A limits an IRA contribution to taxable compensation (W-2 box 1 wages and self-employment earnings; combined on a joint return). seed:2, seed:10, seed:14 and seed:17 contributed to a Roth IRA with a salary of $0; the contribution is now refused and, under the redirect policy, deposited in a taxable account (the owner, 2026-09-26).

changes.change: S5AA R29: a transfer into a 401(k) from a different kind of account is refused
changes.why: Money reaches a workplace plan through payroll, a rollover of the same tax character, or a conversion to the owner's own Roth account (the owner, 2026-09-28: "Refuse it"). seed:9 moved $23,350.60 from an HSA into a traditional 401(k) at 59, three years after retiring; the engine now moves nothing and records TRANSFER_INTO_WORKPLACE_REFUSED, so the HSA keeps the money and the 401(k) does not receive it.

changes.change: S5AA R29, PCF-02: a transfer into an IRA or an HSA from a different kind of account is a contribution
changes.why: Such a transfer is held to the room the year's planned contributions leave (the IRA limit with catch-up, the Roth phase-out and the compensation limit; the HSA self or family limit with catch-up) and deducted as a contribution; under the redirect policy the excess never leaves its source (the owner, 2026-09-28: "As a contribution", "Stays in the source"). seed:4 moved $56,260.18 and seed:13 $54,279.64 from a taxable account into an HSA; only the HSA room now moves, deducted above the line, and the rest stays taxable.

changes.change: S5AA R29: money that leaves a taxable account for a non-taxable one realises its gain
changes.why: Funding an IRA or HSA contribution from a taxable account means selling; the moved dollars realise their gain at the source's pro-rata basis, by the account's owner, as a taxable withdrawal does (found in passing with PCF-02; the owner, 2026-09-28: "Repair in R29"). seed:4 and seed:13 move taxable money into an HSA; what moves now realises its gain.

changes.change: S5AA R32: a catch-up limit reads the age the owner reaches by the row's close
changes.why: The owner, 2026-09-28: "Use the year-end age" (IRC 219(b)(5)(B), 414(v)(5)(A), 414(v)(2)(B)(i), 223(b)(3)(A)). seed:10 and seed:11: the row the owner turns 50 gains the catch-up (+$8,000; +$9,100). seed:20: the row the owner turns 60 gains the 60-63 amount (+$3,250 sheltered instead of redirected) and the row they turn 64 loses it.

changes.change: S5AA R33 commit 1 (SA32F-10, SA32F-28, SA32F-29): the IRA phase-outs reduce the LIMIT, with the 219(g)(2) $10 rounding and $200 minimum; a Roth IRA contribution is the lesser of the reduced limit and the limit less other IRA contributions
changes.why: The four golden plans share the default household (joint filer, $145,000 salary growing 3%, a $7,000 Roth IRA contribution). Its salary proxy crosses the joint Roth range in rows 19 and 20: the Roth limit rounds up to 6,580 (was 6,576.54) and 1,110 (was 1,103.83), hand-checked at a 0% return for each plan; the larger Roth and the smaller redirected taxable excess carry through the later rows

changes.change: S5AA R33 commit 2 (SA32F-11, SA32F-30, SA32F-31): a deferral is excluded only as far as the law excludes it -- from employment-stream and self-employment pay too, never above the owner's own compensation (IRC 415(c)(1)(B)), and never above the limit under the warn policy (402(g)(1)(A))
changes.why: seed:2 and seed:10 plan 401(k) deferrals in working years with NO compensation (salary 0, no employment stream then). The deferral is now 0. seed:10 has no taxable account: its row contributions fall from 28,900 to the 4,400 HSA contribution alone (36,900 to 4,400 from 50). seed:2 redirects the refused deferral to its taxable account, whose dividends raise its AGI (67,641.69 to 68,486.09 in the first row)

changes.change: S5AA R33 commit 4 (SA32F-16): the age-65 amounts -- the additional standard deduction, the senior deduction and Arizona's $2,100 exemption -- read the age reached by the row's close (IRC 63(f)(1)(A), 151(d)(5)(C)(ii)(I), A.R.S. 43-1023(E))
changes.why: In every moved plan the first row that moves is the one in which a living person turns 65 (opens below 65, closes at 65) and its tax falls; checked per plan by overnight/r33/turning65-check.js. golden:baseline's row closing at 65 drops $610.20 = (1,650 x 24% + 2,100 x 2.5%) / (1 - 0.265), the saving grossed up through the pre-tax draw that pays the tax; later rows move through the balances

changes.change: S5AA R33 commit 5 (SA32F-33): a married couple on a single or head-of-household return carries only the self's own 63(f) amount, at the married rate, no spouse amounts and no senior deduction (IRC 151(d)(5)(C)(ii)(II) and (v), 63(f)(1)(B) and (3))
changes.why: seeds 3, 4, 17 and 18 have a spouse and a single or head-of-household status. In the row the self turns 65 the tax rises by 400 (2,050 to 1,650) at the marginal rate: seed:3 +96 (24%), seed:17 +128 (32%), seed:18 +166.04 grossed up. seed:4 (self 67, working, MAGI 3.06M): the total return moves +148 (400 at 37%), while the wage-only baseline loses 3,503.75 of senior deduction plus 400 at 22% (+858.83, measured directly), so the portfolio draws 1,174.92 less and the row's tax falls 316.09 = 148 - 1,174.92 x 39.5%

changes.change: S5AA R33 commit 6 (SA32F-32): the capital-gains worksheet's line 25, the smaller of the preferential and the regular tax, in the estimator and the funding solver's mirror (pwaMin)
changes.why: No control plan's figures change: every row matches the previous commit to within 1e-9 (the Monte Carlo golden plan 1.5e-8), measured by overnight/r33/c6-moves.js. The re-declared values in these nine scenarios differ from the stored declarations only in the last floating-point digits (e.g. 554013.6341638049 against 554013.634163805), from the solver's new min() landing one unit differently

changes.change: S5AA R34 (SA32F-01 to -07, -18, -25; R32V-03): Social Security by law -- the entered benefit in today's dollars with its COLA to the claim, full retirement age from each person's birth year, SSA's rounding, the spouse's benefit, the survivor benefit on the PIA with the widow(er)'s limit, net self-employment earnings and the grace year in the earnings test, and a Social Security stream that ends at its owner's death
changes.why: Traced plan by plan before declaring, R33 engine against R34. (1) SA32F-04, every plan whose claim lies after its start: the PIA takes the COLA from the plan's start to the claim, each step rounded to the dime -- golden:baseline (29.5, claims 67) pays 99,972 at 68 where it paid 36,000 (37.5 years at 2.8%); targeted:historical-1929/1966 take two 2.8% fallback steps (2,113.50, 25,356), historical-2000 takes 2000's 3.5% and 2001's 2.6% (2,123.80, 25,476); seed:11's history opens in 1976 and fifteen historical COLAs take 2,258.30 to 5,438.20 (48,936 at 0.75), matched to the dollar by an independent chain. A claim before the plan's start is indexed from the claim, as before, now rounded: golden:rmd-and-roth-conversion +984 (3,166 a month against 3,084, with 4 months of credit for a 1958 birth). (2) SA32F-05/-25: seeds 4, 5, 6, 10, 16 and 17 carry a jittered ssFra of 66 that R33 read for both people; the birth year gives 67 (66y10m for seed:4's self), so their factors fall (0.8667 to 0.80, 1.24 to 1.16, 0.75 to 0.70, 1.08 to 1.00); seed:5's income drops one year because the 66-67 row is still before full retirement age and the earnings test still withholds; seed:10 is the AIME path, PIA 1,571.60 with one COLA from 62, at 0.75. targeted:historical-spouse-ss/spouse-cola-income: the spouse (67, born 1959) gets 2 months of credit, 1,824 a month; both PIAs take 2020-21's 1.3% and 5.9%: 54,360 at 68, hand-matched. (3) SA32F-03: seeds 6, 14, 18 and 20 have a lower-earning or zero-benefit spouse who now draws the spouse's benefit once both have filed. (4) R32V-03 rounding in every moved plan. The Monte Carlo golden plan moves by the same SS change; its sensitive-band sibling is re-chosen by its declared rule (family version 4, step 26).

changes.change: S5AA R35 commit 2 (SA32F-19): a working spouse's net pay earned after the household's retirement date pays spending before the portfolio
changes.why: Traced against commit 1, first moved row by first moved row. Each moved seed has a younger spouse still on salary after the primary's retirement age, and every move begins in the first retired row the spouse still works: seed:3 (spouse 50, $173,874 salary; row 59-60 withdrawals 184,631.80 -> 51,637.82), seed:4 (spouse 59 works to 75 on the self's clock; from row 75-76), seed:16 (spouse 52; from row 57-58, 61,464.77 -> 31,635.00), seed:17 (Monte Carlo; spouse 50 at $165,395 to 61; success 4.17% -> 8.33%), seed:18 (spouse 40 at $59,427; from row 58-59). The portfolio's incremental tax is still drawn; the net pay after the wage-only tax and the pay-funded contributions offsets spending, capped at the spending.

changes.change: S5AA R35 commit 3 (SA32F-36, decision 6): fixed-nominal spending is today's dollars grown to the retirement date, then held
changes.why: Traced against commit 2. The two control plans on fixedNominal with a deferred retirement move from their first retired row. seed:16 (54, retiring 57, inflation 3.43%): the base grows by the three years to 57 (spending 26,722.24 -> 28,749.01 in row 57-58). seed:20 (59, retiring 69, inflation 5.3%): the base grows by ten years, 34,244.87 -> 57,396 (x1.676), and its 61.56% percent stage (69-76) takes 35,333 of it every row; with the stage removed the old engine spends a flat 34,245 and the new 57,396, measured. Its old rows varied (21,673; 26,521; 29,348) because surplusPolicy 'spend' spent outside-income surplus on top of the small staged amount; the larger base now absorbs that surplus and the portfolio pays the incremental tax.

changes.change: S5AA R35 commit 6 (SA32F-37, R32V-01): the prior-period return signal and VPW's pacing rate are the portfolio's own, balance-weighted
changes.why: Traced against commit 5. golden:monte-carlo-fixed-seed (3 accounts, flexibility 10) and seed:17 (Monte Carlo; a second, taxable account appears at 66, where the moves begin): the unweighted mean of the accounts' draws becomes their balance-weighted return, so a few paths change sign. seed:9 (Monte Carlo VPW with allocations): VPW now paces on the allocations' expected return, and the weighted signal. seed:10 (historical, bond tent on, fee 0.58%): the signal is the accounts' realised rates, net of the fee and the tent, not the bare market series. targeted:historical-spouse-ss and spouse-cola-income hold no accounts: there is no portfolio return, so history's 2022 loss no longer cuts their spending (flexibility 10): row 68-69 62,366.61 -> 69,296.23.

changes.change: S5AA R35 commit 10 (SA32F-22): the Rule of 55 needs a separation in or after the year of 55
changes.why: Traced against commit 9. seed:1 switches the Rule of 55 on but retired at 53, so under IRC 72(t)(2)(A)(v) its 401(k) draws before 59 1/2 are not exempt. Its first moved row is the one opening at 59: the optimized order no longer takes the (formerly exempt) 401(k) and draws the HSA instead (preTax 2,211,982.85 -> 2,235,466.31; hsa 362,962.40 -> 339,679.72; that row's tax 200.77 -> 0).

changes.change: S5AA R36 (SA32F-D1, the owner's decision 8 and D8): later tax years index the 2026 figures -- price-linked amounts by the plan's inflation, wage-linked by the salary-growth field, each with its statute's rounding; statutory fixed amounts fixed
changes.why: Traced against R35 (26ef26d), every plan: plan year 0 (the 2026 rules) is untouched in all 28, and each first moves in tax year 1 or later, in tax-linked fields (taxes, withdrawals, and the balances they drive) -- tax year 1 for 23 of them; seed:1 in year 7, seed:12 in year 9, and the historical 1929, 1966 and 2000 plans in years 16, 4 and 3. Row yi is tax year 2026 + yi, a partial first row included, so the golden plans (opening at 29.5) first move in the row opening at 30. targeted:historical-spouse-ss, targeted:spouse-cola-income and targeted:survivor-stateful do not move. A public-route test pins a later year to the cent by hand (5,099 in 2026, 5,020.75 in 2027 at 3%). Golden regenerated.

changes.change: S5AA R37 (SA32F-27, SA32F-35, SA32F-38): plan warnings -- the 1959 RMD warning for a spouse, a filing status that does not fit the household (a warning, the recommendation of record), and an expense at or after the plan's end age
changes.why: Only the issues list moves: each named plan gains exactly one WARNING and no figure changes. Checked plan by plan against its inputs: 11 plans file jointly with no spouse included (the five golden plans, the three historical plans, arm-flag-on and the two collision plans -- the app's default plan is itself mfj with spouseOn false) and 6 file single or head of household with a spouse included (seed:3, 4, 13, 14, 17, 18), each FILING_HOUSEHOLD_MISMATCH; seed:12 has an expense at age 59 with endAge 59, EXPENSE_AFTER_PLAN_END. No control plan has a spouse born in 1959. Golden regenerated, unchanged: it carries no issues.

changes.change: S5AA R40 repair 1: the long-term-care cost grows at healthcare inflation from the plan's start (the insurance benefit stays as entered)
changes.why: Predicted before the edit in audit/S5AA/R40/S5AA_R40_PREDICTION_RECORD_20260930.md section 1: row spending rises by cost x ((1 + healthInflation)^(open - start) - 1) x overlap x probability in each care row. changes.change: S5AA R40 repair 2: each person on Medicare pays the 2026 Part D base beneficiary premium, $38.99 a month (CMS, July 28, 2025; 42 CFR 423.286(c)), not only its IRMAA surcharge
changes.why: Predicted before the edit in audit/S5AA/R40/S5AA_R40_PREDICTION_RECORD_20260930.md section 2: row spending rises by 467.88 x people on Medicare x retired duration. seed:10: exactly +467.88 in each row where its constant-percent strategy does not react (72, 78 on), and less in 73 to 77 where the lower balance lowers that strategy's own spending, as the record said it might. seed:16: its surplus policy is spend, so the premium displaces spent surplus and no figure moves beyond the last binary digit (seven spending values differ at about 1e-10 from the changed order of the sum).

changes.change: S5AA R42 (R41F-01): a worker's earnings-test excess is charged against the family's benefits on the worker's record, then the spouse's own excess against what is left (POMS RS 02501.095 B.4)
changes.why: seed:20 row 67 (self 66-67, spouse 62): the self's excess withholds 6,058.09, less than the self's own 27,360, and the spouse's own excess withholds the spouse's whole 13,356. Charged over the family pool of 31,548 (the self's own and the spouse's 4,188 spousal part), 804.21 of the self's withholding falls on the spousal part, which the spouse's own excess then cannot charge again; household withholding falls from 19,414.09 to 18,609.88, so Social Security rises 804.21 and every later figure follows. Measured after the repair: the prediction (550764b) excluded rows where the spouse's own test already withholds the whole spousal part, which under SSA's order still move.
